paragraphs.source_en: “There is no harm in being dissatisfied. If dissatisfaction arises, let it arise; then for a while your heart will feel easier. People are of all sorts; even if you want others to be just like yourself, they will not become so. With chopsticks, unless you hold them as other people do, eating naturally becomes difficult. Bread, however, is the most convenient thing. You may cut it any way you please. A skillful tailor will bring you clothes that fit as soon as you put them on; with clothes made by a poor tailor, you can only make do and wear them as they are. But the world is an amusingly well-arranged place. As you go on wearing them, the clothes themselves naturally come to fit your bones. If your capable parents had skillfully given birth to a you who suited this present world, you would of course be happy. But if they could not produce such an ideal you, then you must either go on living out of step with the times, or endure until you can adapt yourself to society. There is no other road to take.” The visitor revealed the face of a philosopher.
